title: Contextual header microinteractions and accessible drag handles across density modes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and specification for header-level microinteractions: reveal-on-hover contextual affordances (sort, filter, column actions), persistent accessible drag handles for column resize/reorder, and consistent behavior across compact/regular/comfortable density modes. Deliver a developer-facing spec (tokens, CSS classes, interaction states) and an accessibility test plan.
background: Recent front-end work introduced three density modes and a new virtualized renderer. Engineers report inconsistencies where header affordances disappear in compact density and keyboard focus order changes between densities. Designers have also received requests to make column drag/resize handles usable on touch and keyboard-first flows without visual clutter. Current implementations are inconsistent across apps and cause UX regressions during rollouts.
design_goals: Make header actions discoverable but minimally intrusive in all densities
Provide keyboard-first and screen-reader-friendly drag/resize affordances
Ensure affordances survive virtualization (not lost during rapid mount/unmount)
Expose clear tokens and CSS hooks for engineering to implement without layout hacks
Keep motion subtle and performant on low-end devices
constraints: Must work with the existing virtualized row renderer and column virtualization. Avoid adding extra DOM nodes per cell where possible. Interaction must respect user preference for reduced motion and high-contrast modes. Implementation should not rely on experimental CSS that isn't supported in Chromium and WebKit stable releases.
exploration_notes: We explored three reveal patterns: always-visible minimal icons, hover-reveal, and focus-reveal. Research sessions with two PM teams preferred focus-reveal (keyboard-first) combined with subtle hover reveal for pointer users. Touch users need persistent affordances: we propose a short press-to-open menu on header title or an always-present thin handle in compact mode.
tradeoffs:
- Always-visible icons increase visual noise in dense tables but simplify touch support.
- Hover-only reveal reduces clutter but breaks keyboard discoverability if not paired with focus styles.
- Adding persistent handles may add DOM complexity and can affect virtualization unless implemented as a single overlay layer managed by the table runtime.
decisions: Adopt focus-reveal as primary accessibility-first pattern (keyboard users see actions on focus).
Add hover-reveal for pointer users with a 120ms delay to avoid flicker during quick cursor passes.
Introduce a single overlay handle layer controlled by the table runtime to provide persistent touch handles without duplicating DOM per header cell.
Expose three new tokens: --table-header-affordance-opacity, --table-handle-hit-area, --table-drag-handle-color, and document fallbacks for older themes.
implementation_notes: Spec details for engineers: Provide ARIA: header button elements must have aria-controls and aria-expanded where relevant. Drag handles should be keyboard-focusable with role='separator' and use aria-orientation='horizontal'. A single overlay should be positioned with absolute layout and pointer-events managed to funnel events to the appropriate column index. For virtualization, handle overlay updates will be debounced to 8ms and synchronized with KV-cache culling to avoid jitter.
tasks: Finalize wireframes for each density (compact, regular, comfortable)
Produce Figma component variants and export token mappings
Write developer spec (CSS classes, ARIA requirements, JS integration pattern)
Coordinate with infra/serving runtime owners to implement overlay pattern in table runtime
Create accessibility test plan and run 5 manual audits with VoiceOver/JAWS and keyboard-only flows
Validate performance: column interactions maintain 60fps on mid-tier laptop (Intel i5) and 30fps on low-end mobile
links: Previous ticket (engineering): ENG-84210 - table runtime overlay prototype
acceptance_criteria: Figma file contains annotated component variants for all three densities with clear token mapping
Developer spec includes CSS variables, classes, and an example JS integration for the overlay handles
Keyboard-only flow: tab to header reveals actions and drag handle; resizing via keyboard (arrow keys + modifier) works and is announced by screen readers
Touch flow: long-press on header title opens contextual menu; thin persistent handle in compact mode activates resize/reorder on drag
Performance tests show <16ms frame time during typical header drag on mid-tier laptop and <50ms on low-end mobile
Accessibility audit: 0 critical issues; any remaining minor issues have remediation tickets assigned
